title: Experiment credentialing and decision tree (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notes doc to capture a lightweight credentialing checklist + decision tree for cross-functional canary and A/B experiments. The goal is to speed up safe launches by making the minimum gating explicit and reproducible (who signs off, what staging checks are mandatory, and what thresholds force an immediate rollback).

Audience:
- PMs and product engineers running rollout experiments
- SRE/Obs on-call and reliability engineers
- Privacy/security reviewer for model/data handling
- Solutions/SEs supporting customer-facing canaries (Dedicated/Private)

Summary / One-liner:
A compact credentialing flow that maps experiment risk -> required evidence -> decision action (proceed / restrict slice / abort) and a small rollback matrix with contact points and initial mitigation steps.

Quick glossary (shorthand used below):
- Cohort: an audience slice for exposure
- Tier: customer/traffic tier (free, paid, enterprise)
- SLI: service-level indicator (latency, errors, cost per token)
- Obsv: observability dashboards and traces

Credentialing checklist (minimum evidence to start a canary):
1) Feature spec and hypothesis: short doc + target metric(s) (owner: PM).
2) Safety & content review: annotated prompt examples + safety verdict (owner: Safety).
3) Privacy/data usage sign-off: doc listing any user data used in evals and retention policy (owner: Privacy).
4) Model pin and fallbacks: model sha/tag pinned for canary, compatible fallback model identified and smoke-tested (owner: ML infra).
5) Budget cap set: hard token/egress budget and automatic throttle if exceeded (owner: Finance/Cost ops).
6) Ops playbook: postmortem contact list, throttles, and runbook snippet added to the experiment ticket (owner: Eng / SRE).
7) Canary exposure plan: cohort selection, percentage slices, duration per slice, escalation windows (owner: PM).
8) Observability hooks validated: traces, per-route SLI dashboards, alert rules (owner: Observability).

Credentialing notes / open questions:
- Do we require a distinct "security smoke test" for private deployments? Suggest yes for on-prem (network, KMS integration).
- For high-cost models, add a precondition: burst-only for first 24h with manual approval to increase capacity.
- Should solutions/SEs be listed as approvers for customer-facing experiments on Dedicated? (Might be required for enterprise customers.)

Decision tree (compact, textual):
Start -> Risk tier assessment -> if Risk=Low then run auto-canary (no exec approver) else require Exec or Security approver.
Risk tier heuristics:
- Low: internal-only or non-customer visible metric tweaks; model variants with no new data exposures.
- Medium: customer-visible behavior change, new model version with similar training domain.
- High: PII handling, new tool-calling surface, model-generated actions (e.g., transactions).

Decision nodes and actions (examples):
- Metric degradation > 5% in primary SLI within 30m -> immediate slice reduction to 10% and paging to on-call.
- Cost per token > 2x expected for sustained 15m -> throttle traffic to budget cap and notify finance.
- Safety regression flagged by eval set (automated) -> pause canary AND initiate manual safety review.

Stop conditions (automatic):
- 3 critical errors per minute on experiment route for 10 minutes
- Latency p95 > target+250ms for more than 15 minutes
- Customer complaint triage: 2 verified complaints from enterprise customers in canary slice

Rollback matrix (starter template):
- Partial rollback (preferred): shift traffic to fallback model variant within same route (fast path).
- Full rollback: disable new route and revert to previous routing policy (requires SRE + PM).
- Emergency outage rollback: global disable switch (on-call SRE or platform lead).

Comms checklist (what to say when pausing/reverting):
- Short status (what happened, when, users impacted)
- Safe fallback in place and user-facing impact (if any)
- Next steps and ETA for recover/next check-in
- Links: experiment ticket, obs dashboard, relevant logs

Runbook snippet (to paste into experiment ticket):
- Title: [Experiment X] credentialing snapshot
- Owner(s): {PM, Eng, SRE}
- Start time (planned): YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
- Canary slices: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 48h (canary window for each step: 12h)
- Critical SLIs: latency p95, err rate, safety-regression-rate, cost per 1k tokens
- Immediate actions on trigger: reduce slice -> switch model -> page on-call -> run forensic log dump

Practical heuristics and heuristics to harden choice of cohorts:
- Prefer deterministic cohorting (user-id hash) over geo or cookie-based for reproducibility.
- Avoid mixing enterprise customers and new model variants in first exposure pulse.
- Use multiple micro-cohorts for internal dogfooding before external slices.

Checklist for Observability ownership (quick):
- Per-route SLIs wired into alerting channel
- One dashboard with a single time window controlling experiment view
- Synthetic probes validating prompt->response path every 5 minutes
- Token-level cost chart with rolling 1h window and threshold alert

Operational notes (TBD / TODOs):
- Build a small "credentialing form" in the Console to collect evidence items above; tie to experiment metadata.
- Add an auto-assessment step that maps filled form to an initial risk tier suggestion.
- Small helper script to snapshot model pin + rollback URL and attach to ticket automatically.
- Formalize emergency communication template for customer success to use when customers notice regressions.

Example scenarios (short):
1) Low-risk UI prompt tweak: auto-canary, no exec sign-off, 24h window.
2) Medium-risk model update affecting routing: PM + SRE + Safety sign-off; 48h incremental rollout; canary budget cap at 10k tokens.
3) High-risk tool-calling feature: Security + Privacy + Legal sign-off; initial internal-only cohorts for 72h then gated external exposure.

Notes to collaborators (meta):
- Rohit: can you sketch the Console form fields to capture the checklist?
- Maya: can you propose minimal set of synthetic probes for the safety pipeline?
- Liam: can SRE outline the fast-switch path for fallback models (1-liner steps)?

References and links:
- Experiment taxonomy doc (WIP): CON-1234
- Rollout telemetry patterns: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/rollout-telemetry
- Related runbooks in this folder: look up "risk-budgeting-and-observation-playbook-wip" (for overlap)

Unresolved decisions (to discuss in kickoff):
- Thresholds for "metric degradation" need firming (absolute vs relative).
- Whether credentialing is mandatory for internal-only experiments (pro: consistency, con: friction).

End of working notes.

-- Ava M (PM, product console)
